title: Moments of inertia of upper/middle/lower trunk (vertebral boundaries) by CT

quantity.name: segment moment of inertia about CM
quantity.definition: Icm about transverse (x), antero-posterior (y), longitudinal (z) axes through segment CM

source.authors: Pearsall DJ, Reid JG, Livingston LA
source.sample: 4 hospital-referred adults (2 male, 2 female), serial transverse CT at 1-cm intervals pubic symphysis to T1, supine
source.age: 61.0 y (individuals 46, 65, 68, 65; printed SD 1.0 is inconsistent with individual ages)
source.notes: height SD 13.8, mass SD 6.7, BMI 24.4 (2.4). DOI not printed (likely 10.1007/BF02667349 – verify). Subjects referred for medical reasons (pathology judged not to affect results).

protocol.summary: Icm of trunk subsegments; Table 3 values are in thousands of kg·cm² (text: whole trunk 7,100, 8,200, 3,100 kg·cm²).
how_to_use: Use whole-trunk Icm_x 0.71 kg·m² (7,100 kg·cm²) about the medio-lateral axis for sagittal trunk dynamics; 'kg_m2' field gives the conversion.

measurement.device: GE CT/T Continuum (Hi Light Advantage); pixel intensity calibrated to tissue density
measurement.posture: supine, upper limbs in anatomical position

protocol.notes: Vertebral-level segments bounded through the intervertebral discs (each contains one complete vertebral body); upper (thorax) = T1-T12, middle (abdomen) = L1-L5, lower (pelvis) = S1-S5 (pubic symphysis); trunk = T1-S5. Neck and upper limbs (lateral to glenohumeral joint) and lower limbs (lateral to hip joint) excluded. NOTE: these boundaries differ fundamentally from Pearsall 1994/Zatsiorsky/de Leva (landmark-based) trunk subsegments.

extraction.check_notes: Table 3 lists e.g. 7.1, 8.2, 3.1 for the whole trunk; text states 7,100, 8,200, 3,100 kg·cm², confirming the ×10³ kg·cm² unit.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
